question: While calculating the volume of a cone, its radius is measured $1\%$ greater and its height $2\%$ greater than their actual values. Estimate the percentage error in the calculated volume and justify its sign.
explanation:
Volume relation
The volume of a cone is
$$V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h$$
Relative differential
Taking the relative change,
$$\frac{dV}{V}=2\frac{dr}{r}+\frac{dh}{h}$$
Substitution of percentage errors
The radius has a positive error of $1\%$ and the height has a positive error of $2\%$. Therefore,
$$\frac{dV}{V}\times100=2(1\%)+2\%$$
$$=4\%$$
Sign interpretation
Both measurements are greater than their actual values, so both contributions to the volume error are positive.
Conclusion
The calculated volume has an approximate positive error of $4\%$ and is therefore overestimated.

options.A: $4\%$ positive error; the volume is overestimated
options.B: $3\%$ positive error; the volume is overestimated
options.C: $4\%$ negative error; the volume is underestimated
options.D: $2\%$ positive error; the volume is overestimated
